symptom: External hosts cannot read referenced skill files and standard prompt arguments do not bind identity.
direct_cause: MCP exposes only SKILL.md body and reads identity from nonstandard top-level prompt fields.
class_root: MCP projections do not preserve the canonical content-addressed skill package boundary.
affected_population: Verified MCP hosts reading multi-file skill packages

external_sources.purpose: Standard arguments and metadata extension points
Content-addressed URI resources and textual content

invariants: Every exposed file belongs to the authorized package and current content hash.
Prompt identity travels through standard arguments and metadata.
generality_proof: Both prompt and resource entry points use skillStore package visibility, hash and safe file-map lookup; no filesystem paths from MCP are opened directly.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Authorize package and verify its file-map hash before returning any file.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Passes parsed identity and relative file path through skills.read.
Standard arguments are validated before the same skills.read boundary.

recurrence.reason: Any multi-file package or conforming MCP host can hit this boundary.
same_class_scan: Inspected readSkillContentForMcp and listSkillSummariesForMcp in skillStore.ts.
Inspected resources/read and prompts/get in mcpProtocol.ts and laneInstalledSkills.mts package roots.

prevention.invariant: Only authorized current package files are readable.
prevention.failure_mode: Stale hash, unsafe or absent path and unauthorized audience return null.
prevention.strategy: Derive file metadata and content from existing safe package reader and hash.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove top-level prompt identity fields; standard arguments own the input.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Internal protocol projection using existing MCP standard; no new dependency.

migration: Root resource URIs remain stable. Prompt callers use advertised standard arguments; no stored data migration.
residual_risks: Only files supported by canonical text skill packages are exposed; binary media remains outside that format.
